A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoSca, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A-G, whereas v2 ends after its references and points to supplemental material that is not supplied. This limits comparison of some implementation and optimization details.

before.justification: v1 reports original DyCheck and NVIDIA rendering results, component ablations, qualitative reconstructions, and appendix optimization diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 reports original rendering experiments, camera-pose and correspondence evaluations, component and foundation-model ablations, and application demonstrations.

M1.justification: v2 removes v1's DINO-based trajectory filtering and semantic dragging, adds rendered tracking supervision to photometric optimization, and replaces rendering-error-based node densification with tracking-loss-gradient-based densification. It also introduces foreground-to-background Gaussian copying and opacity resetting. These change the reconstruction procedure substantially, although the scaffold, ARAP regularization, and global Gaussian fusion remain.

E1.justification: DyCheck and NVIDIA rendering coverage is retained. v2 adds camera-pose evaluation on Sintel and TUM-dynamics, correspondence evaluation on DyCheck, and application demonstrations involving foreground removal, occluder removal, semantic rendering, and editing. Its qualitative examples also expand beyond v1's DAVIS and SORA examples to movie and internet videos.

E2.justification: The DyCheck comparison adds Dynamic Gaussians, 4DGS, Gaussian Marbles, DpDy, D-NPC, and Shape-of-Motion; NVIDIA adds D-NPC and Gaussian Marbles. New camera and correspondence comparisons include SLAM/odometry methods and trackers such as MonST3R and BootsTAPIR. RoDynRF/RobustDynrf and DynPoint/DyPoint are retained methods under varying names.

E3.justification: DyCheck uses BootsTAPIR in v2 instead of v1's CoTracker-v2. v2 adds a five-scene, 1x-resolution Shape-of-Motion comparison and a pose-free variant with supplied focal length. New evaluations use ATE/RPE and PCK-T. Fusion ablations change from percentages of timesteps to four or eight neighboring frames. The newly stated standard 2x resolution does not establish a change to the original benchmark resolution.

E4.justification: v2 adds a tracker-by-depth-model ablation matrix and a tracking-loss ablation, and quantifies node-control and skinning-correction effects previously illustrated qualitatively. It revises temporal-fusion experiments while retaining geometric optimization, photometric optimization, DQB, and topology ablations. v1's semantic-feature and canonical-reference ablations, along with its appendix optimization diagnostics, are not included in the supplied v2.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Scene averages and feature-variance calculations do not constitute repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The full-model DyCheck aggregate changes from 18.44/0.648/0.227 to 19.32/0.706/0.264 for mPSNR/mSSIM/mLPIPS. NVIDIA mean PSNR changes from 26.55 to 26.72. These are revised-system results, not isolated same-setting gains. v2 adds substantial camera, correspondence, and ablation results, including PCK-T 0.824, while omitting v1's per-scene benchmark breakdowns and GOF results.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives change: v1's explicitly defined semantic loss and its geometric-objective contribution disappear, while v2 adds tracking loss to the photometric objective. The scaffold, curve-distance, and ARAP formulations largely persist. The DQB formula in v2 Section 3.1 already appeared in v1 Appendix B; neither version supplies new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: a sparse motion scaffold combines foundation-model priors with physical regularization, globally fuses dynamic Gaussians, supports unknown cameras, and achieves strong dynamic-rendering performance. v2 foregrounds automation and real-world use, but these do not materially extend the earlier claimed scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a concrete limitation concerning shadows, reflections, liquids, and exposure changes that deformation alone cannot explain. It interprets the new RGB-only depth ablations as showing the benefit of LiDAR information. The principal explanations involving global fusion and sparse regularization, and the limitations involving prior quality and never-visible regions, remain.

D1.justification: v1 supplies node-resampling and staged-optimization details plus a 16 GB GPU requirement and approximately 0.5-2-hour fitting time in its appendices. These details are unavailable in the supplied v2. v2 adds resolution information and Table 7's rendering-speed and representation-size measurements, and changes the abstract's future code-release promise to a project-and-code pointer. Actual external availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions MoSca against concurrent MoDGS, DynOMo, Gaussian Marbles, and Shape-of-Motion using its structured deformation representation and automated pipeline. It also substantially expands the cited camera-estimation, tracking, and depth literature accompanying the new evaluations. Some earlier semantic-tracking references disappear. These changes extend the substantive comparison context beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The method is reorganized into a deformation representation followed by an ordered reconstruction pipeline, placing camera initialization before geometric lifting. The DQB explanation moves from Appendix B into the main text. The introduction and experimental narrative are extensively revised, including new camera/correspondence and applications subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redesigns the overview and qualitative displays, and replaces the extensive per-scene benchmark tables with compact aggregate comparisons and explicit setting groups. It adds camera, correspondence, prior-ablation, specification, and application displays. The earlier appendix diagnostic figures are absent from the supplied v2.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the reconstruction pipeline through direct camera and correspondence evaluations, stronger comparison coverage, and foundation-prior ablations. It also acknowledges a concrete lighting-related failure boundary. These gains are tempered by the absence of v1's implementation appendices and per-scene benchmark breakdowns, which reduces reproducibility and diagnostic detail in the supplied PDF. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement; the changed rendering scores alone do not establish improvement.
